ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
title: Can You Remove an Out of Bounds Post?
question: Your ball comes to rest next to a white out of bounds post. The post is stopping you from making a full swing. Can you remove the post to play your shot?

choices.text: Yes, because it is an artificial object and therefore a movable obstruction.
Yes, but only if you replace it before leaving the hole.
No. Out of bounds posts are boundary objects and must not be moved to improve your shot.
Yes, but you must add one penalty stroke.

explanation: White out of bounds posts are boundary objects, not obstructions. Boundary objects are treated as fixed parts of the course and no free relief is available from them. Players must not move or remove a boundary object to improve the conditions affecting their stroke. Even if a boundary object is movable (such as a removable fence panel or gate), it is still treated as a boundary object when defining the course boundary and must not be moved. (Rule 8.1a and the Definition of Boundary Object)

juniorVersion.title: Can You Move an Out of Bounds Post?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball stops next to a white out of bounds post. The post is in the way of your swing. Can you move the post so you can hit your ball?

choices.text: Yes, because it is man-made and you can move it.
Yes, but only if you put it back after you play.
No. Out of bounds posts are part of the course and must not be moved.
Yes, but you must add one penalty shot.

juniorVersion.explanation: White out of bounds posts show the edge of the golf course. They are not just things you can move. You must not move or take away an out of bounds post to make your shot easier.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A white post that shows where the golf course ends.
Something like a post or fence that marks the edge of the course and cannot be moved.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind juniors that out of bounds posts are not like sticks or stones. They are special and must stay in the ground.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think it’s okay to move a post to help their swing.
Children may believe if they put the post back, it is allowed.
